ownership.quote: the team behind Codeanywhere is back with a new venture called Daytona

stage.quote: Daytona has raised a $24M Series A led by FirstMark Capital to build the infrastructure that makes this possible.
stage.note: Founders previously built Codeanywhere (2013, Croatia); Daytona (2023) is a new venture from the same team. Not a YC company (ycombinator.com/companies/daytona returns 404); no accelerator/incubator participation found. Last priced round is the Feb 2026 $24M Series A.

total_funding_usd.basis: sum of $2M pre-seed (Nov 2023, TechCrunch/company blog) + $24M Series A (Feb 2026, company blog), both primary-sourced
total_funding_usd.quote: Daytona has raised a $24M Series A led by FirstMark Capital

last_round.quote: Daytona is backed by FirstMark Capital, with participation from Pace Capital, Upfront Ventures, Darkmode, and E2VC, as well as strategic investments from Datadog and Figma Ventures.

revenue.basis: company blog post claiming this made Daytona the fastest-growing infrastructure company in history
revenue.quote: Two months later, we crossed $1M in ARR. We believe this makes Daytona the fastest-growing infrastructure company in history, from zero to $1M ARR in just about 2 months.

note: Founders (Ivan Burazin CEO, Vedran Jukic CTO, Goran Draganić) previously built Codeanywhere (cloud IDE, from 2013). Daytona pivoted from an open-source enterprise dev-environment (CDE) product to an agent-native sandbox/runtime platform around April 2025, hitting $1M ARR ~2 months after that relaunch (by July 2025). The originally open-source daytonaio/daytona GitHub repo (AGPLv3, frozen at v0.190.0) is now unmaintained: core development moved to a private/closed-source codebase as of June 2026. Matt Turck (FirstMark) joined the board with the Series A.
